subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards remain full-content-only, or should OpenClaw add a narrowly documented opt-in append/transport mode for deployments where full-content CardKit updates are too slow?
rationale: The evidence now points at a real latency regression, but the known alternatives trade off CardKit’s full-content contract against responsiveness and may affect existing Feishu deployments differently.

options.title: Require Feishu Owner Decision On Payload Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask the Feishu owner to choose the permanent contract after live proof compares full-content, coalesced full-content, and append behavior for both latency and truncation.

options.title: Keep Full-Content Only
options.body: Reject append mode and continue pursuing a CardKit-compatible full-content mitigation, accepting that affected deployments may stay slow until a better approach is proven.

options.title: Add Opt-In Append Mode
options.body: Add a documented per-account opt-in mode with tests and live proof, while preserving full-content as the default for setups that truncate suffix-only updates.

recommendation.title: Require Feishu Owner Decision On Payload Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask the Feishu owner to choose the permanent contract after live proof compares full-content, coalesced full-content, and append behavior for both latency and truncation.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata names this handle as the Feishu plugin maintainer, and the decision is specific to Feishu CardKit behavior.
